summary: Gradual throughput degradation results in SSE client timeout during extended multi-turn chat
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports progressive slowdown in token throughput for long, multi-turn SSE chat sessions. After ~30–90s of apparent generation, the stream becomes quiet (no data chunks) and the client eventually hits a read timeout. Impact: Conversations truncate mid-response and clients observe socket timeouts. This affects a subset of sessions on Dedicated pools and reproduces for both redwood-llama-13b-v2 and mpt-7b-chat under sustained multi-turn traffic.

Impact: End-user messages appear stuck mid-generation; UX shows spinner until client-side timeout. Not broad outage but frequent for NoteStream's heavy long-context workflows, causing increased error rates and support tickets.

Environment: Dedicated capacity pool d-nyc-02, prod us-east-1, running serving-runtime 1.12.4 with streaming-proxy 0.8.2 and api-gateway 2.4.1. Customer sessions originate from a single IP block behind a corporate proxy.

Observed behavior: Throughput (tokens/sec) degrades gradually across a long response; the server continues to run model but emitted chunk rate drops to near-zero. Server-side logs show repeated small GC pauses and occasional client-side backpressure warnings from the streaming-proxy. After ~60–120s of low emission rate, edge connection is closed with a 499/timeout at the proxy.

Expected behavior: Continuous token emission at normal per-token latency for the configured model profile; keepalive heartbeats or chunked-keepalive should prevent client timeout during temporary micro-degradation.

Temporary workaround: Customer increased client read timeout from 30s to 120s and observed fewer disconnects. We suggested pinning to a non-quantized model variant and enabling KV-cache warmup to reduce cold evictions.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create a long multi-turn chat session with a 4-6 turn history and a final user prompt expecting long generated continuation (~800-1200 tokens).
2) Use SSE endpoint with default client read timeout (30s).
3) Observe token emission rate from server logs and client-side SSE events. Run under sustained load (10 concurrent long sessions) on Dedicated pool d-nyc-02.
4) Compare behavior against a short prompt (50 tokens) to confirm degradation is correlated with long context generation.
logs: 2026-03-05T15:12:50Z runtime[worker-12]: KV-cache eviction triggered for session=se-772 (cold page swap), pause=85ms
2026-03-05T15:14:12Z proxy[edge]: connection closed by client after idle_timeout (499)
comments: 2026-03-05 15:30 - Support (Ava Martinez): Reached out to customer for full session IDs and sample SSE trace. Customer provided two sample session IDs and confirmed increasing client timeout mitigates frequency.

2026-03-06 09:12 - SRE (Liam Chen): Reproduced locally in staging by simulating sustained KV cache pressure; observed cumulative token latency climbing from 40ms to 400ms over ~45s before emission gaps.

2026-03-07 11:45 - Eng (Maya Patel): Noted an interaction between the new eviction policy (release-window tuning) and streaming-proxy backpressure: eviction-induced pauses were longer than expected when combined with IO scheduling on the pod.
2026-03-10 17:05 - Support (Ava Martinez): Customer confirmed reduced error rate after increasing read timeout and applying recommended warmup; asked for ETA on permanent fix.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: KV-cache cold evictions under sustained multi-turn workloads cause blocking pauses in runtime that are not properly smoothed by the streaming pipeline.
Hypothesis 2: Streaming-proxy interprets long inter-chunk gaps as client backpressure and deprioritizes the connection, aggravating pause durations until proxy enforces idle-close.

Finding: Traces show worker thread experiencing GC-like pauses during memory compaction and page migration (worker-12). Pause durations correlate with token_emit_rate drops. Proxy metrics show queued buffers per-connection spike concurrently.
Load repro in staging: applying a patch to limit eviction compaction decreased pause durations from ~80–150ms to ~10–30ms and eliminated most observed timeouts in 1h stress run.
resolution_notes: Mitigation deployed 2026-03-09: Reverted aggressive eviction compaction flags in serving-runtime 1.12.4 -> 1.12.4-hotfix.1 and adjusted streaming-proxy keepalive threshold to 45s for Dedicated pools. Rollout targeted d-nyc-02 initially.
Customer impact: NoteStream reported a 92% reduction in SSE timeouts for affected workflows after hotfix and client-timeout increase.

Follow-up actions: 1) Engineering to implement non-blocking KV-cache migration (RFC created). 2) Add server-side proactive keepalive events when per-token emission rate drops below threshold. 3) Add automated alerting for token_emit_rate dropouts on Dedicated pools.
